1	// Copyright (c) 2026 Benjamin Borbe All rights reserved.
2	// Use of this source code is governed by a BSD-style
3	// license that can be found in the LICENSE file.
4	
5	// Command github-dark-factory-agent is the canonical AI-heavy agent: one Claude
6	// invocation per phase, all logic in the prompt + allowed tools.
7	//
8	// This binary is the Kafka entry point — spawned as a K8s Job by
9	// task/executor with TASK_CONTENT + TASK_ID + PHASE + KAFKA_BROKERS env.
10	// For local CLI mode (file-based), see cmd/run-task/main.go.
11	//
12	// Reference implementation for AI-heavy agents using the agent framework
13	// (lib.NewAgent + claude.NewAgentStep). Other agents (trade-analysis,
14	// pr-reviewer) follow the same shape — copy this main.go and swap
15	// prompts/tools.
16	package main
17	
18	import (
19		"context"
20		"os"
21		"time"
22	
23		agentlib "github.com/bborbe/agent"
24		claudelib "github.com/bborbe/agent/claude"
25		delivery "github.com/bborbe/agent/delivery"
26		"github.com/bborbe/agent/envparse"
27		libmetrics "github.com/bborbe/agent/metrics"
28		"github.com/bborbe/cqrs/base"
29		"github.com/bborbe/errors"
30		libkafka "github.com/bborbe/kafka"
31		githubapp "github.com/bborbe/maintainer/githubapp"
32		libsentry "github.com/bborbe/sentry"
33		"github.com/bborbe/service"
34		libtime "github.com/bborbe/time"
35		"github.com/bborbe/vault-cli/pkg/domain"
36		"github.com/golang/glog"
37		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus"
38		"github.com/prometheus/client_golang/prometheus/push"
39	
40		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/factory"
41		"github.com/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent/pkg/githubauth"
42	)
43	
44	// agentName is the identity string used for Prometheus metric grouping and logging.
45	const agentName = "github-dark-factory-agent"
46	
47	func main() {
48		app := &application{}
49		os.Exit(service.Main(context.Background(), app, &app.SentryDSN, &app.SentryProxy))
50	}
51	
52	type application struct {
53		SentryDSN   string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-dsn"   env:"SENTRY_DSN"   usage:"SentryDSN"    display:"length"`
54		SentryProxy string `required:"false" arg:"sentry-proxy" env:"SENTRY_PROXY" usage:"Sentry Proxy" display:"length"`
55	
56		// Claude Code CLI configuration
57		ClaudeConfigDir claudelib.ClaudeConfigDir `required:"false" arg:"claude-config-dir" env:"CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR" usage:"Claude Code config directory"`
58	
59		// Agent directory (contains .claude/ with CLAUDE.md and commands)
60		AgentDir claudelib.AgentDir `required:"false" arg:"agent-dir" env:"AGENT_DIR" usage:"Agent directory with .claude/ config" default:"agent"`
61	
62		// Allowed tools (comma-separated)
63		AllowedToolsRaw string `required:"false" arg:"allowed-tools" env:"ALLOWED_TOOLS" usage:"Comma-separated list of allowed tools"`
64	
65		// Task content from agent pipeline
66		TaskContent string `required:"true" arg:"task-content" env:"TASK_CONTENT" usage:"Raw task markdown from vault"`
67	
68		// Environment context passed to prompt (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs)
69		EnvContextRaw string `required:"false" arg:"env-context" env:"ENV_CONTEXT" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for prompt context"`
70	
71		// Environment variables passed to Claude CLI process (comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs).
72		// Use this for ad-hoc / less-common env vars. The three load-bearing Anthropic provider
73		// vars below have dedicated arg slots so they don't have to be packed into this string.
74		ClaudeEnvRaw string `required:"false" arg:"claude-env" env:"CLAUDE_ENV" usage:"Comma-separated KEY=VALUE pairs for Claude CLI environment"`
75	
76		// Anthropic-compatible provider routing. Setting AnthropicBaseURL + AnthropicAuthToken
77		// routes the claude CLI to an alt-provider (e.g. MiniMax via https://api.minimax.io/anthropic).
78		// AnthropicModel drives both the `--model` CLI flag and the ANTHROPIC_MODEL env var seen by
79		// the claude subprocess. Non-empty values override the same keys in ClaudeEnvRaw.
80		AnthropicBaseURL   string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-base-url"   env:"ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"   usage:"Anthropic-compatible API base URL"`
81		AnthropicAuthToken string                `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-auth-token" env:"ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN" usage:"Bearer token for ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"                                  display:"length"`
82		AnthropicModel     claudelib.ClaudeModel `required:"false" arg:"anthropic-model"      env:"ANTHROPIC_MODEL"      usage:"Model name; also exposed to the claude subprocess as ANTHROPIC_MODEL"                  default:"sonnet"`
83	
84		// Branch for Kafka result delivery
85		Branch base.Branch `required:"false" arg:"branch" env:"BRANCH" usage:"branch"`
86	
87		// TopicPrefix is an explicit Kafka topic prefix, independent of Branch.
88		TopicPrefix base.TopicPrefix `required:"false" arg:"topic-prefix" env:"TOPIC_PREFIX" usage:"Explicit Kafka topic prefix; empty means unprefixed topics"`
89	
90		// Phase to run (framework requires explicit phase)
91		Phase domain.TaskPhase `required:"false" arg:"phase" env:"PHASE" usage:"Agent phase: planning | execution | ai_review" default:"execution"`
92	
93		// GitHub token for authenticated clones + REST API calls (planning phase).
94		// Used as the raw fallback credential when GitHub App creds are absent
95		// (local cmd/run-task path where the operator exports `gh auth token`).
96		GhToken string `required:"false" arg:"gh-token" env:"GH_TOKEN" usage:"GitHub token for clone + PR inspection (raw fallback when App creds unset)" display:"length"`
97	
98		// GitHub App authentication. When APP_ID, INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file
99		// or inline) are all set, the pod mints a short-lived installation access
100		// token at startup and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess as GH_TOKEN.
101		// The cluster pod sets these (GH_TOKEN is empty there); locally they are
102		// absent and the agent falls back to the raw GhToken above.
103		AppID          int64  `required:"false" arg:"app-id"          env:"APP_ID"          usage:"GitHub App ID (numeric); enables App auth when set with INSTALLATION_ID + PEM"`
104		InstallationID int64  `required:"false" arg:"installation-id" env:"INSTALLATION_ID" usage:"GitHub App Installation ID (numeric)"`
105		PEMKeyFile     string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key-file"    env:"PEM_KEY_FILE"    usage:"Path to the GitHub App private key (PEM file mounted from k8s Secret)"`
106		PEMKey         string `required:"false" arg:"pem-key"         env:"PEM_KEY"         usage:"GitHub App private key (PEM) as env var content; mutually exclusive with PEM_KEY_FILE" display:"length"`
107	
108		// Workdir paths for bare-clone cache and per-task worktrees.
109		ReposPath string `required:"false" arg:"repos-path" env:"REPOS_PATH" usage:"Root path for bare-clone cache"   default:"/repos"`
110		WorkPath  string `required:"false" arg:"work-path"  env:"WORK_PATH"  usage:"Root path for per-task worktrees" default:"/work"`
111	
112		// Kafka delivery (optional — only active when TASK_ID is set)
113		KafkaBrokers libkafka.Brokers        `required:"false" arg:"kafka-brokers" env:"KAFKA_BROKERS" usage:"Comma separated list of Kafka brokers"`
114		TaskID       agentlib.TaskIdentifier `required:"false" arg:"task-id"       env:"TASK_ID"       usage:"Agent task identifier for publishing results back to task controller"`
115	
116		PushgatewayURL string `required:"false" arg:"pushgateway-url" env:"PUSHGATEWAY_URL" usage:"Prometheus PushGateway URL"          default:"http://pushgateway:9090"`
117		TaskType       string `required:"false" arg:"task-type"       env:"TASK_TYPE"       usage:"Task type label for metric grouping" default:"unknown"`
118	}
119	
120	func (a *application) Run(ctx context.Context, _ libsentry.Client) error {
121		registry := prometheus.NewRegistry()
122		jobMetrics := libmetrics.NewJobMetrics(registry, libtime.NewCurrentDateTime())
123		pusher := push.New(a.PushgatewayURL, libmetrics.BuildJobMetricsName(agentName)).
124			Grouping("agent", agentName).
125			Grouping("task_type", a.TaskType).
126			Collector(registry)
127		defer func() {
128			if err := pusher.PushContext(ctx); err != nil {
129				glog.Warningf("prometheus push failed: %v", err)
130				return
131			}
132			glog.V(2).Infof("prometheus push completed")
133		}()
134		start := libtime.NewCurrentDateTime().Now().Time()
135	
136		glog.V(2).Infof("github-dark-factory-agent started phase=%s", a.Phase)
137	
138		// Resolve the GitHub credential (App IAT or raw GH_TOKEN fallback) and make
139		// it usable by every git/gh subprocess. See prepareAuth.
140		resolvedToken, err := a.prepareAuth(ctx)
141		if err != nil {
142			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
143			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
144			return err
145		}
146	
147		deliverer := delivery.NewNoopResultDeliverer()
148		if a.TaskID != "" {
149			if len(a.KafkaBrokers) == 0 {
150				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
151				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
152				return errors.Errorf(ctx, "KAFKA_BROKERS must be set when TASK_ID is set")
153			}
154			syncProducer, err := factory.CreateSyncProducer(ctx, a.KafkaBrokers)
155			if err != nil {
156				jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
157				jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
158				return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "create sync producer")
159			}
160			defer func() {
161				if err := syncProducer.Close(); err != nil {
162					glog.Warningf("close sync producer failed: %v", err)
163				}
164			}()
165			deliverer = factory.CreateKafkaResultDeliverer(
166				syncProducer, a.TopicPrefix, a.TaskID, a.TaskContent,
167				libtime.NewCurrentDateTime(),
168			)
169		}
170	
171		claudeEnv := a.buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken)
172	
173		repoManager := factory.CreateRepoManager(a.ReposPath, a.WorkPath, resolvedToken)
174		githubClient := factory.CreateGitHubClient(resolvedToken)
175		claudeProber := factory.CreateClaudeProber(a.ClaudeConfigDir)
176		provider := factory.CreateAgentProvider(
177			a.ClaudeConfigDir,
178			a.AgentDir,
179			a.AnthropicModel,
180			resolvedToken,
181			claudeEnv,
182			repoManager,
183			githubClient,
184			claudeProber,
185			// Re-mint before the push: the installation token is minted once here at
186			// startup and expires after 60 minutes, but a lifecycle run routinely
187			// takes longer, so the final push would be refused as an invalid token.
188			a.resolveAuth,
189		)
190		agent, err := provider.Get(ctx, agentlib.TaskType(a.TaskType))
191		if err != nil {
192			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
193			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
194			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "select agent for task_type")
195		}
196	
197		result, err := agent.Run(ctx, a.Phase, a.TaskContent, deliverer)
198		if err != nil {
199			jobMetrics.RecordRun(agentlib.AgentStatusFailed)
200			jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
201			return errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "agent run failed")
202		}
203		jobMetrics.RecordRun(result.Status)
204		jobMetrics.RecordDuration(time.Since(start))
205		return finishRun(ctx, result, a.Phase)
206	}
207	
208	// finishRun publishes the agent's result and then decides the Job's exit code.
209	// It exists as one call so Run stays within its funlen budget.
210	func finishRun(
211		ctx context.Context,
212		result *agentlib.Result,
213		phase domain.TaskPhase,
214	) error {
215		if err := agentlib.PrintResult(ctx, result); err != nil {
216			return err
217		}
218		return exitErrorForStatus(ctx, result.Status, phase)
219	}
220	
221	// exitErrorForStatus returns a non-nil error when the agent's published status
222	// must fail the Job, and nil when the Job may exit 0.
223	//
224	// A failed result is still published to the task, but the Job must also exit
225	// non-zero. The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded
226	// in agent-task-executor's job_watcher), so returning nil here makes a failed run
227	// indistinguishable from a completed one: the failure is written as a phase
228	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at human_review
229	// as though a human had parked it deliberately (2026-11-03, task ceb79961: a Job
230	// that published Status=failed for a git clone error exited 0 and parked the
231	// task).
232	//
233	// needs_input is deliberately NOT a failure: parking for a human answer is that
234	// status's intent, and it reaches the same park path on purpose.
235	func exitErrorForStatus(
236		ctx context.Context,
237		status agentlib.AgentStatus,
238		phase domain.TaskPhase,
239	) error {
240		if status == agentlib.AgentStatusFailed {
241			return errors.Errorf(
242				ctx,
243				"agent reported status %q for phase %q",
244				status,
245				phase,
246			)
247		}
248		return nil
249	}
250	
251	// buildClaudeEnv assembles the Claude CLI subprocess env from the raw env
252	// pairs plus the Anthropic provider-routing overrides. resolvedToken, when
253	// non-empty, is threaded in as GH_TOKEN — the ai_review phase's Claude
254	// subprocess shells `gh pr view/diff`, and the runner strips pod env to an
255	// allowlist, so the token must be passed explicitly (os.Setenv in prepareAuth
256	// covers the dark-factory daemon path, not the Claude runner).
257	func (a *application) buildClaudeEnv(resolvedToken string) map[string]string {
258		claudeEnv := envparse.KeyValuePairs(a.ClaudeEnvRaw)
259		if claudeEnv == nil {
260			claudeEnv = map[string]string{}
261		}
262		if a.AnthropicBaseURL != "" {
263			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL"] = a.AnthropicBaseURL
264		}
265		if a.AnthropicAuthToken != "" {
266			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN"] = a.AnthropicAuthToken
267		}
268		if a.AnthropicModel != "" {
269			claudeEnv["ANTHROPIC_MODEL"] = a.AnthropicModel.String()
270		}
271		if resolvedToken != "" {
272			claudeEnv["GH_TOKEN"] = resolvedToken
273		}
274		return claudeEnv
275	}
276	
277	// prepareAuth resolves the GitHub credential and makes it usable by every
278	// git/gh subprocess: it exports GH_TOKEN (covering the dark-factory daemon,
279	// which inherits os.Environ() for its `git push`) and installs git's credential
280	// helper via `gh auth setup-git`. Returns the resolved token for the
281	// RepoManager / GitHub client / gh-token preflight wiring.
282	func (a *application) prepareAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
283		resolvedToken, err := a.resolveAuth(ctx)
284		if err != nil {
285			return "", err
286		}
287		// resolvedToken is always non-empty here (resolveAuth errors otherwise), but
288		// guard defensively — an empty GH_TOKEN would mislead the daemon subprocess.
289		if resolvedToken != "" {
290			if err := os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", resolvedToken); err != nil {
291				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "export GH_TOKEN")
292			}
293		}
294		if err := githubauth.NewGhAuthSetupGit(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
295			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "gh auth setup-git")
296		}
297		// A file the daemon re-reads outlives the token bound into gh's helper: the
298		// installation token expires after 60 minutes and the lifecycle daemon keeps
299		// its startup environment, so a long run's own `git fetch` would use a dead
300		// token (2026-11-03, bborbe/trading#433).
301		if err := githubauth.NewFileBackedHelper(resolvedToken).Setup(ctx); err != nil {
302			return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "configure file-backed credential helper")
303		}
304		return resolvedToken, nil
305	}
306	
307	// resolveAuth resolves the GitHub credential forwarded to every git/gh
308	// subprocess. It prefers GitHub App authentication: when APP_ID,
309	// INSTALLATION_ID, and a PEM (file or inline) are all set, it mints a
310	// short-lived installation access token via githubapp.MintIAT. Otherwise it
311	// falls back to the raw GH_TOKEN input — the local cmd/run-task path where the
312	// operator exports `gh auth token`. When neither is configured it returns a
313	// clear error, since the agent cannot clone or push without a credential.
314	//
315	// The token is a runtime value (not a config input), so it is returned to the
316	// caller rather than stored on the argument-parsed application struct —
317	// argument/v2 panics when reflecting over unexported struct fields at startup.
318	func (a *application) resolveAuth(ctx context.Context) (string, error) {
319		hasPEMFile := a.PEMKeyFile != ""
320		hasPEMContent := a.PEMKey != ""
321		useGitHubApp := a.AppID != 0 && a.InstallationID != 0 && (hasPEMFile || hasPEMContent)
322		if useGitHubApp {
323			appCfg := githubapp.Config{AppID: a.AppID, InstallationID: a.InstallationID}
324			if hasPEMFile {
325				appCfg.PEMPath = a.PEMKeyFile
326			} else {
327				appCfg.PEM = []byte(a.PEMKey)
328			}
329			// Startup auth must not be killed by the task's work deadline: mint on a
330			// fresh bounded context (keeps ctx values, drops the caller's
331			// deadline/cancel) so a near-deadline task can't fail the token mint.
332			mintCtx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.WithoutCancel(ctx), 30*time.Second)
333			defer cancel()
334			iat, err := githubapp.MintIAT(mintCtx, appCfg)
335			if err != nil {
336				return "", errors.Wrap(ctx, err, "mint github app iat")
337			}
338			glog.V(2).Infof(
339				"github-dark-factory-agent auth mode=github-app app_id=%d installation_id=%d",
340				a.AppID, a.InstallationID,

20	// TestExitErrorForStatus guards the exit-code contract between this agent and
21	// the executor that watches its Job.
22	//
23	// The executor records a phase success on exit 0 alone (IsJobSucceeded in
24	// agent-task-executor's job_watcher) and never reads the Status this agent
25	// publishes. So a run that reports failure but exits 0 is written as a phase
26	// success, and once the success grace expires the task is parked at
27	// human_review as though a human had parked it deliberately.
28	//
29	// Observed 2026-11-03: task ceb79961 published Status=failed for
30	// "git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443", exited 0, and
31	// parked at human_review.
32	func TestExitErrorForStatus(t *testing.T) {
33		ctx := context.Background()
34		phase := domain.TaskPhase("execution")
35	
36		cases := []struct {
37			name    string
38			status  agentlib.AgentStatus
39			wantErr bool
40		}{
41			{
42				name:    "failed must fail the Job so the executor does not record a phase success",
43				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusFailed,
44				wantErr: true,
45			},
46			{
47				name:    "done exits 0",
48				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusDone,
49				wantErr: false,
50			},
51			{
52				name:    "in_progress exits 0",
53				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusInProgress,
54				wantErr: false,
55			},
56			{
57				// needs_input reaches the same park path on purpose: the task is meant
58				// to wait at human_review for an answer, not to be re-driven.
59				name:    "needs_input exits 0 — parking for a human answer is its intent",
60				status:  agentlib.AgentStatusNeedsInput,
61				wantErr: false,
62			},
63		}
64	
65		for _, c := range cases {
66			t.Run(c.name, func(t *testing.T) {
67				err := exitErrorForStatus(ctx, c.status, phase)
68				if c.wantErr && err == nil {
69					t.Fatalf(
70						"status %q: expected a non-nil error, got nil — the Job would exit 0 and the executor would record it as a phase success",
71						c.status,
72					)
73				}
74				if !c.wantErr && err != nil {
75					t.Fatalf("status %q: expected nil, got %v", c.status, err)
76				}
77			})
78		}
79	}
80	
81	// TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken guards the startup argument dump against
82	// republishing the ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN value into the Job log.
83	//
84	// argument.Print honours only display:"hidden" and display:"length"; every other
85	// tag value falls through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`). The root
86	// binary's application struct carried display:"password" — a value the printer does
87	// not implement — so each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in
88	// cleartext. This test drives the real printer over the real struct, so removing
89	// the display:"length" tag turns it red.
90	//
91	// Plain testing rather than Ginkgo on purpose: application is unexported, so the
92	// assertion must live in package main, and package main_test (main_test.go) shares
93	// this test binary — where a second RunSpecs fails with "calling RunSpecs more than
94	// once". An internal spec therefore cannot join the existing suite. Same shape as
95	// TestExitErrorForStatus above.
96	func TestPrintRedactsAnthropicAuthToken(t *testing.T) {
97		const sentinel = "sentinel-token-do-not-log-9f3a2b7c1d"
98	
99		var buf bytes.Buffer
100		log.SetOutput(&buf)
101		log.SetFlags(0)
102		defer func() {
103			log.SetOutput(os.Stderr)
104			log.SetFlags(log.LstdFlags)
105		}()
106	
107		if err := argument.Print(context.Background(), &application{AnthropicAuthToken: sentinel}); err != nil {
108			t.Fatalf("print: %v", err)
109		}
110	
111		rendered := buf.String()
112		if got := strings.Count(rendered, sentinel); got != 0 {
113			t.Fatalf(
114				"token value leaked into the argument dump: sentinel appeared %d times\n%s",
115				got,
116				rendered,
117			)
118		}
119		if got := strings.Count(rendered, "AnthropicAuthToken"); got != 1 {
120			t.Fatalf("want the field named exactly once, got %d\n%s", got, rendered)
121		}
122		if !strings.Contains(rendered, "Argument: AnthropicAuthToken length ") {
123			t.Fatalf("want the length form, got:\n%s", rendered)
124		}
125	}

8	## v0.6.2
9	
10	- fix: link the pinned dark-factory clone to `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/dark-factory` so the authoring-rule paths the agents hardcode resolve — a local-path `marketplace add` never creates that directory, so prompt generation ran with no guides

12	## v0.6.1
13	
14	- chore: restate the `do-not-merge` gate message to name its bypass actors — the Admin repository role and Integration `3907226`, both `bypass_mode: always` in the `master-protection` ruleset — instead of asserting an unqualified block
15	
16	## v0.6.0
17	
18	- feat: **build the release image on a cluster (`BUILD_TARGET=sun`), not only locally.** `make build` had a single arm — a local `docker build` — so publishing a release required a Docker daemon and `docker push` on the workstation. An agent is refused `docker push`, which made a release image unpublishable without a human at the keyboard. `Makefile.docker` now carries two arms, ported from `bborbe/a2a-worker-controller` and `bborbe/agent-claude`: `BUILD_TARGET=local` (the default, unchanged behaviour) and any other value, which renders `hack/build-job.yaml` as a Job on that cluster and pushes from inside it. The vendored `hack/` set is `a2a-worker-controller`'s hardened copy — templated namespace, `case`-based value whitelisting, no service-account token — rather than `agent-claude`'s older one. The cluster arm refuses to run without an explicit `VERSION` (the Makefile default is the newest release tag, so a defaulted build would overwrite a published image with one built from a different commit) and refuses to push a `vX.Y.Z` tag from any `REF` other than that tag. `upload` and `clean` are guarded so a remote build does not fail at a push step for an image that was never local. `Dockerfile` gains a `go mod vendor` step in its build stage: the local arm got `vendor/` from `check-go-mod`, but the cluster arm clones a git ref where `vendor/` is gitignored, so `-mod=vendor` would have failed there. `make precommit` now runs `shellcheck -S warning` over `hack/*.sh`, since those scripts handle the teamvault→Secret credential path
19	
20	## v0.5.14
21	
22	- fix: **redact the `AnthropicAuthToken` value from the startup argument dump.** The root binary's `application` struct carried `display:"password"` — a tag the argument printer does not implement. It honours only `display:"hidden"` and `display:"length"`, so every other value fell through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`) and each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in cleartext into the cluster Job log. The field now carries `display:"length"`, matching the sibling in `cmd/run-task`, so the dump names the key and its length and never the value. A regression spec drives the real printer over the real struct and fails if the redaction is removed
23	
24	## v0.5.13
25	
26	- test: **cover the per-prompt setup fetch, not only the push.** `v0.5.12` moved the credential to a file-backed git helper, but only the push site had a regression spec — the fetch site (the one that failed first on 2026-11-03) was pinned by nothing. The new spec starts with token `A`, lets the lifecycle refresher mint `B`, and asserts the credential `git credential fill` resolves *during* the run is `B` — the A→B shape a "file is non-empty" check would not discriminate. No production code changes
27	
28	## v0.5.12
29	
30	- fix: **install a file-backed git credential helper so a long lifecycle run never uses an expired token.** The GitHub App installation token lives 60 minutes and is minted once at startup; `gh auth setup-git` binds it into a helper that resolves `GH_TOKEN` from the environment of whatever runs git, and the dark-factory daemon captured that environment when it was started — so no refresh in the parent process can reach it. A token file has no such lifetime: git re-reads it at every credential lookup. Observed 2026-11-03 on `bborbe/trading#433`: token minted 18:10Z, the daemon's own `git fetch origin` refused at 19:15Z with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported`
31	
32	## v0.5.11
33	
34	- fix: **exit non-zero when the agent publishes `Status: failed`.** The result was still published to the task, but the process returned nil, so the Job completed and the executor — which records a phase success on exit 0 alone (`IsJobSucceeded` in `agent-task-executor`'s `job_watcher`) and never reads the published Status — wrote a *phase success* for a run that had failed. Once the success grace expired the task was parked at `human_review` as though a human had parked it deliberately. Observed 2026-11-03 on task `ceb79961`: a Job that published `Status: failed` for `git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443` exited 0 and parked the task. `needs_input` is deliberately unchanged — parking for a human answer is that status's intent

40	## v0.5.9
41	
42	- fix: re-mint the GitHub credential immediately before the push. The installation token is minted once at startup (`resolveAuth` → `githubapp.MintIAT`) and GitHub App installation tokens expire after 60 minutes, while the execution phase routinely runs longer — so the final `git push` was refused with `remote: Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported for Git operation`, after the implementation itself had succeeded. Measured 2026-11-02 on `bborbe/attention-controller#166`: token minted 14:54Z, push attempted 16:07Z, 73 minutes later. The execution step now calls a `refreshToken` seam right before `PushBranch` and exports the fresh value into the process env the push inherits; a refresh failure is logged and the step continues, so a short run that still holds a valid token is unaffected. The credential consumers that captured the startup token — `pkg/git`'s `cmdEnv()` and the GitHub REST client — now read the live `GH_TOKEN` first, so the refresh also reaches `headAfterPush` and ai_review's own `GetPullRequest` / worktree fetch, not only the push. **Not covered:** ai_review's Claude subprocess still receives the startup token, because its env map is built once from `resolvedToken` and the Claude runner applies an allowlist rather than inheriting `os.Environ()`. That path only matters if the review model shells `gh pr view/diff` after the 60-minute mark; the review step's own REST and git calls use the refreshed token. (`Permission to … denied` would have meant the App lacked write access — it did not, which is what ruled that out.)

46	- fix: pass the egress proxy environment through to git subprocesses. `cmdEnv()` returned only `HOME`, `PATH` and `GH_TOKEN`, so a clone from a sandbox that admits egress only through the allowlisting proxy dialled `github.com:443` directly and was refused by the NetworkPolicy in 2–9 ms — every dark-factory run on nuke prod failed at `planning: ensure worktree` before any LLM work started. The six proxy variables (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and their lowercase forms) are appended when set, mirroring `github-pr-review-agent`, `github-releaser-agent` and `github-update-go-agent`, which took the same fix on 2026-10-28; an unset variable still contributes no entry, so the allowlist does not become a pass-through.

50	- fix: update github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.132.5 (with cqrs v0.6.13, errors v1.6.4, kafka v1.28.6, sentry v1.10.6, time v1.27.18, vault-cli v0.178.3 pulled in transitively) so the result deliverer stops restoring a stale phase. A result that advances no phase no longer republishes the Job-start phase over a park: the Kafka payload omits `phase` on those branches, so the controller's on-disk-first merge keeps the on-disk value, and the file deliverer carries the on-disk phase forward. Closes the prod-vs-sun duplicate class measured on v7.

52	## v0.5.6
53	
54	- fix: fail a lifecycle run that is stranded in **any** non-terminal spec status, not only `prompted`. `drained()` accepts only `verifying`/`completed`, but the stall detector compared against `prompted` alone, so a spec left at `draft` or `approved` kept `drained()` false forever while nothing could advance it — the daemon logged `nothing to do, waiting for changes` and the run held its only agent slot until `activeDeadlineSeconds: 5400`. Measured 2026-10-22 17:28Z→18:34Z: spec `063-a2a-default-cluster` sat at `verifying` while a sibling spec never advanced, **45 idle iterations over ~66 min**, on v0.5.5 — a build that already contained every earlier guard, which is why the previous grace-window fix did not cover it. The detector now skips only `verifying`/`completed`/**`generating`** and reports any other status with no prompt in flight. `generating` stays excluded deliberately: dark-factory drives it and `runner/lifecycle.go` resumes or resets it after a restart, so aborting there would kill healthy work — and while **any** spec under `specs/in-progress` is `generating`, nothing is reported at all, because dark-factory generates prompts one spec at a time (`specWatcher` mutex + sequential startup scan), so a sibling legitimately waits at `approved` for the whole generation (~7 min). Flagging that sibling would abort a healthy multi-spec run 30 s in. `stallGracePolls` 3 → 10 (30 s at the 3 s poll) because `draft`/`approved` have no prompt to watch, so the grace must outlast the daemon's own pickup tick as well as the `prompted` flicker — still turning a 90-minute slot-hold into 30 seconds. The error now names the spec's real status instead of hard-coding `prompted`.
55	
56	## v0.5.5
57	
58	- fix: skip the ai_review worktree post-conditions when execution adopted an already-pushed branch. The adopt path routes to ai_review without creating a worktree, but ai_review checked out the task's stale `ref` and demanded every matched spec be completed there — completions the original run had already pushed to the branch, so the check could never pass and every adoption ended in `spec … is not completed (execution did not finish)`. Found on the nuke-dev replay: the run logged `"adopted": true` and then failed one step later. An adopted result now goes straight to the read-only PR verdict; the draft-PR and diff-vs-spec checks still run. Its `## Review` records only those two in `checks_passed` (with `adopted: true`) — not the `specs_completed` / `no_prompts_in_flight` gates the adopted path never evaluates, since that artifact is the human's draft→ready sign-off and must not attest to checks that did not run.

62	- fix: adopt an already-pushed branch head instead of re-running the whole lifecycle. A crash after `PushBranch` but before `## Result` is delivered left the remote branch ahead of the task's `ref`; the re-run repeated the full LLM job (~30 min of prompts, reproduced on nuke dev 2026-10-21) and then failed non-fast-forward with `! [rejected] HEAD -> <branch> (non-fast-forward)`, leaving a spurious failed task. The execution step now compares the remote branch head with `ref` before `EnsureWorktree`: a head that moved **and** descends from `ref` is adopted (no lifecycle, `## Result` written citing the head with `adopted: true` and `prompts_executed: 0`); a head that moved but does not descend from `ref` returns needs-input naming both shas rather than claiming another push's work.

Both are resolved via `ResolveLifecycleTimeoutFromEnv` / `ResolveLifecycleTimeout` and threaded through `NewExecutionRunnerWithTimeout`. Invalid/absent values fall back safely (never zero).
116	- fix: handle ignored `os.Setenv`/`os.Unsetenv` error returns in the lifecycle-timeout tests so the standalone errcheck target passes.
117	- fix: unexport `resolveLifecycleTimeoutFromEnv`/`resolveLifecycleTimeout` (factory-pattern rule — internal helpers, test access via `export_test.go` aliases) and lowercase the env-parse warning messages, per bot review.
118	
119	## v0.3.11
120	
121	- chore: update Go to 1.26.6 and dependencies; fix GO-2026-5841 (klauspost/compress), GO-2026-6179 (golang.org/x/mod), GO-2026-6180 (golang.org/x/mod), GO-2026-5026 (stdlib), GO-2026-5972 (stdlib), GO-2026-6090 (stdlib), GO-2026-6218 (stdlib)
122	
123	## v0.3.10
124	
125	- fix: fail-fast on a permanently-failed prompt instead of hanging to the lifecycle deadline. When a dark-factory prompt exhausts its retries the failure handler leaves it in `prompts/in-progress` with `status: failed` and the scanner skips it forever ("queue blocked until manual retry"), so its spec can never reach `verifying`. `drained()` could not distinguish that dead prompt from a slow one, so `waitForDrain` spun until the 30-minute `lifecycleTimeout` — and in-cluster the overall-run budget hard-killed the Job with `context canceled` at ~30 min BEFORE the step could escalate, so no `## Failure` was ever written and the task was not cleanly parked. `waitForDrain` now scans `prompts/in-progress` each tick via new `findFailedPrompt` and returns a lifecycle error the moment a prompt reaches terminal `status: failed`, surfacing its `lastFailReason`. The execution step then escalates cleanly (`Status: failed`) within seconds while the context is still alive — PR stays draft, spec stays incomplete, task parks. Approved/executing/unparseable prompts are ignored (only terminal `failed` counts). Unit tests cover the detector's discrimination + the RunLifecycle fast-path timing.
126	
127	## v0.3.9
128	
129	- fix: commit the spec-completion move before pushing, so completed specs actually reach the PR branch. `dark-factory spec complete` (which the execution step drives after the daemon stops) rewrites the working tree — moving the spec `specs/in-progress → specs/completed` — but does NOT git-commit it (nothing commits it once the daemon is gone, unlike the daemon's per-prompt `workflow:direct` commits). `PushBranch` is a bare `git push HEAD`, so the completion was silently dropped: the PR kept an approved-not-completed spec, the watcher re-emitted the task on the agent's own push, and runs overlapped indefinitely (self-trigger loop). New `ExecutionRunner.CommitSpecChanges` stages `specs/` and commits after `completeSpecs` and before `PushBranch` (no-op when nothing is staged). Now the completed spec lands on the branch → the watcher stops re-triggering → clean multi-spec drain to `human_review`. Unit tests cover the commit + the no-op path and assert the execution step calls it before pushing.
130	
131	## v0.3.8
132	
133	- fix: `RunLifecycle` no longer stops the dark-factory daemon while a generated prompt is still awaiting auto-approval. The drain check (`drained()`) only looked at `prompts/in-progress`, ignoring the generation **inbox** (`prompts/*.md` at the repo root, where a freshly generated prompt waits for the daemon's auto-approve audit). Because the daemon flips the spec to `verifying` while that audit runs, `drained()` returned true mid-audit, `stopDaemon` SIGKILLed the in-flight audit subprocess (`auto-approve: audit FAILED ... signal: killed`), the prompt was never approved/executed, and the implementation file (e.g. the `HELLO_DARK_FACTORY.md` marker) was never created — ai_review then correctly escalated on the absent file. New `hasInboxPrompts` gates the drain on the inbox too, so the lifecycle waits for the prompt to be approved → executed → completed. Surfaced on go-skeleton PR #40 (master `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`, making the audit slow enough to lose the race). Unit test drives a stub daemon that leaves a prompt in the inbox and asserts the lifecycle does not drain.
134	
135	## v0.3.7
136	
137	- fix: inject the fleet model into the backend:local daemon. The execution step now forwards the configured model (`claudelib.ClaudeModel`, from the pod's `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) to `dark-factory daemon` as `--set model=<model>` via `NewExecutionStep`'s new constructor arg — no `os.Getenv` inside the step. The daemon resolves its model from `--set` > `.dark-factory.yaml` `model:` > a built-in Claude default; because it does NOT read `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` for its own selection, a target repo whose `.dark-factory.yaml` omits `model:` silently ran on Sonnet (a ToU violation), which on go-skeleton PR #40 produced a prompt asserting the wrong byte count and never committed the marker. Injecting the model makes the fleet model authoritative regardless of per-repo config. Unit test asserts the flag is forwarded.
138	
139	## v0.3.6
140	
141	- fix: ai_review no longer flags dark-factory's own bookkeeping as out-of-scope. The read-only diff-vs-spec reviewer (`pkg/prompts/review.md`) now excludes pipeline-metadata paths — `prompts/**`, `specs/**`, and `.dark-factory.yaml` — from its scope judgment, since the lifecycle necessarily commits them on every run (generated prompts, in-progress→completed moves). Previously a correct implementation escalated to `failed` at ai_review because a spec constraint like "No other file is modified" can never hold for this pipeline (observed in cluster E2E: the marker was created correctly but the reviewer flagged the prompt/spec churn). The reviewer now judges only real implementation files against the spec. Verified via the local `cmd/run-task` loop against a clean draft PR: the same scenario now returns `pass` → `human_review`.
142	- chore: `go mod tidy` records `github.com/maxbrunsfeld/counterfeiter/v6` as an indirect dependency.
143	- chore: bump `golang.org/x/text` v0.38.0 → v0.39.0 (indirect) — clears CVE-2026-56852 (infinite loop on invalid input) flagged by trivy.
144	
145	## v0.3.5
146	
147	- chore: bump baked `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION` v0.192.0 → v0.192.4 (CLI + plugin). v0.192.4 fixes the `generate-prompts-for-spec` command's hardcoded `/workspace` paths (docker-mount convention) → cwd-relative, so backend:local generation writes prompts into the worktree the daemon watches instead of an empty `/workspace`. Unblocks the backend:local generation→execution lifecycle.
148	
149	## v0.3.4
150	
151	- fix: populate remote-tracking refs (`refs/remotes/origin/*`) in the RepoManager's bare clone. `git clone --bare` maps remote branches to `refs/heads/*`, so `origin/master` never resolved in a worktree — and dark-factory's per-prompt "sync with default branch" (`git merge origin/<default>`, run by every workflow) failed with `origin/master - not something we can merge`, stalling execution after generation. New `configureRemoteTracking` sets the standard `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*` refspec and fetches, on both the clone and update paths.
152	
153	## v0.3.3
154	
155	- fix: bake the `coding` plugin into the runtime image (Dockerfile), alongside the existing `dark-factory` plugin. dark-factory's generation step invokes the prompt-creator agent, which uses the `coding` plugin's Go guides to write prompt files; without it the fleet's MiniMax model (`MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`) produced no prompt file ("generation produced no prompt files") and the spec never left `approved`. Local runs generate fine because the operator's `~/.claude` already has `coding`; the cluster image did not. Mirrors github-pr-review-agent's build-time `coding` install.
156	
157	## v0.3.2
158	
159	- fix: stream the `dark-factory` daemon's stdout/stderr to the agent's own stdout in `dark_factory_runner.startDaemon` (was `cmd.Stdout/Stderr = nil`, i.e. discarded). The backend:local lifecycle — and the claude subprocesses the daemon spawns — is now visible in `kubectl logs`. Without it a hung daemon (e.g. a claude call blocking on a no-TTY onboarding prompt) was indistinguishable from slow progress until the 30-minute lifecycle deadline. Writes to the process stdout/stderr, not a repo file, so it is not swept into the daemon's commits.
160	
161	## v0.3.1
162	
163	- fix: hoist `ARG CLAUDE_YOLO_IMAGE` to global scope (before the first `FROM`) in the Dockerfile. It was declared inside the build stage, so the runtime `FROM ${CLAUDE_YOLO_IMAGE}` could not interpolate it and BuildKit aborted with "base name should not be blank" — `make buca` failed before any push. CI runs `make precommit` (go build/test/lint), never `docker build`, so this latent bug surfaced only on the first real image build.
164	- fix: build the dark-factory CLI from the pinned clone (`go install .` in the module root) instead of `go install github.com/bborbe/dark-factory@${DARK_FACTORY_VERSION}`. dark-factory's `go.mod` carries `exclude` directives, which `go install pkg@version` refuses; building from the module root honors them (same as upstream `make install`). Reuses the clone the runtime image already makes for the plugin marketplace, so there is now a single pinned clone for both CLI and plugin. Both fixes verified with a local `make build`.
165	
166	## v0.3.0
167	
168	- feat: add GitHub App authentication. When `APP_ID`, `INSTALLATION_ID`, and a PEM (`PEM_KEY_FILE` or `PEM_KEY`) are all set, the agent mints a short-lived installation access token at startup (`githubapp.MintIAT`) and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess — `os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", …)` covers the dark-factory daemon's `git push` (inherits `os.Environ()`), `gh auth setup-git` installs the git credential helper, and the token is threaded into the RepoManager, GitHub REST client, and gh-token preflight. Falls back to the raw `GH_TOKEN` input when App creds are absent so local `cmd/run-task` (with `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`) keeps working; errors clearly when neither is configured. Fixes cluster clone/push failures where the pod set no `GH_TOKEN`. Copies `pkg/githubauth` (the `gh auth setup-git` configurator) from github-pr-review-agent.
169	
170	- fix: add `--set hideGit=true` to the execution step's dark-factory flags — the RepoManager runs the lifecycle in a git worktree (`.git` is a file), which trips dark-factory's spec-084 worktree safety gate; without this the daemon refuses to start. Validated in the local E2E: the daemon now starts and runs inside the worktree.
171	- fix: install the dark-factory Claude PLUGIN in the runtime image (Dockerfile), not just the CLI binary. The backend:local lifecycle runs `/dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` and `/dark-factory:audit-prompt` *inside* claude; with only the CLI installed, claude reports `Unknown command` → zero prompts generated → the spec silently resets to `approved` and the daemon idles (the E2E root cause, 2026-07-13). Mirrors github-pr-review-agent's build-time `coding` plugin install. **Pinned** to the same `${DARK_FACTORY_VERSION}` tag as the CLI (clone that tag + add as a local marketplace, not marketplace HEAD) so the plugin minor cannot drift from the CLI minor. Confirmed locally: with the plugin installed, generation produces a valid prompt.
172	- docs: record two backend:local provisioning requirements in design.md Part 5 — (1) the dark-factory plugin must be installed in the runtime `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; (2) backend:local ignores dark-factory `config.env`, so the model-router `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + auth token must be pod env vars (a spec-104 follow-up gap).
173	
174	## v0.2.0
175	
176	- feat: implement Increment 1 of the three-phase implementer — wire planning/execution/ai_review as distinct phases (domain.TaskPhase constants), route the `dark-factory-implement` task type; add RepoManager (bare-clone cache + per-task worktree), claude-auth + gh-token preflight steps, and the pure-Go planning step (clone + precondition scan: ref==PR head, PR draft, `.dark-factory.yaml` present, approved-not-completed spec in the PR diff → writes `## Plan`, routes execution; escalates without mutating assignee/status); wire `cmd/run-task` as a local per-phase harness. Execution/ai_review are stubs (Increments 2/3).
177	- feat: implement Increment 2 — the execution step drives the dark-factory backend:local lifecycle. Live investigation established the correct one-worktree invocation: `dark-factory daemon --set backend=local --set autoGeneratePrompts=true --auto-approve-prompts --skip-preflight --skip-healthcheck` (backgrounded → poll-until-drained → kill; one-shot `run` does NOT generate — generation is daemon-only), then `dark-factory spec complete <id>` (no auto-complete), then `git push`. Adds `pkg/dark_factory_runner.go` (`ExecutionRunner` seam over daemon/spec-complete/push) and replaces the execution stub: idempotent (`## Result` present → route ai_review), config via `--set`/flags never committed to the branch, fail-closed when a spec never reaches `verifying`/`completed` (prompt failed DoD/audit), writes typed `## Result`, routes ai_review — all without mutating assignee/status.
178	- feat: implement Increment 3 — the ai_review step (custom verdict-routing, read-only). A deterministic gate re-checks post-conditions (PR still draft, every matched spec completed, no prompts in-flight) and escalates (`failed`) on violation; then a read-only Claude diff-vs-spec review emits a typed `## Review` verdict. Pass → `Done, human_review` (the human's draft→ready flip is the sign-off); concerns → `failed` (escalate). NEVER runs `gh pr ready`; never clears assignee (the controller does at human_review). Completes the three-phase implementer agent logic (planning → execution → ai_review).
179	
180	## v0.1.3
181	
182	- docs: mark the local-executor dependency RESOLVED in design.md and record the backend:local live-smoke findings — happy path (claude in-process, real commit, zero containers) + the HOME-sensitive claude-auth requirement the Job pod must satisfy
183	
184	## v0.1.2
185	
186	- chore: bump dark-factory CLI to v0.192.0 (ships spec 104 `backend: local` in-process executor) so the agent runs dark-factory without spawning nested containers (no DinD); select at runtime with `--set backend=local`
187	
188	## v0.1.1
189	
190	- refactor: converge build to bborbe/kafka-topic-reader publish-only model — make buca publishes docker.io/bborbe/github-dark-factory-agent:$(VERSION); deploy machinery removed.
191	
192	## v0.1.0
193	
194	- feat: adopt cqrs v0.6.0 / agent v0.72.0 explicit `base.TopicPrefix`; add optional `TopicPrefix` config (`env TOPIC_PREFIX`) for Kafka result topic naming — empty means unprefixed topics (Octopus per-stage clusters), non-empty preserves `develop`/`master` names (quant)
195	- chore: bump `github.com/bborbe/agent` v0.70.0 → v0.72.0, `github.com/bborbe/cqrs` v0.5.2 → v0.6.0
196

# Changelog

All notable changes to this project will be documented in this file.

The format is based on [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com/en/1.0.0/),
and this project adheres to [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org/spec/v2.0.0.html).

## v0.6.2

- fix: link the pinned dark-factory clone to `~/.claude/plugins/marketplaces/dark-factory` so the authoring-rule paths the agents hardcode resolve — a local-path `marketplace add` never creates that directory, so prompt generation ran with no guides

## v0.6.1

- chore: restate the `do-not-merge` gate message to name its bypass actors — the Admin repository role and Integration `3907226`, both `bypass_mode: always` in the `master-protection` ruleset — instead of asserting an unqualified block

## v0.6.0

- feat: **build the release image on a cluster (`BUILD_TARGET=sun`), not only locally.** `make build` had a single arm — a local `docker build` — so publishing a release required a Docker daemon and `docker push` on the workstation. An agent is refused `docker push`, which made a release image unpublishable without a human at the keyboard. `Makefile.docker` now carries two arms, ported from `bborbe/a2a-worker-controller` and `bborbe/agent-claude`: `BUILD_TARGET=local` (the default, unchanged behaviour) and any other value, which renders `hack/build-job.yaml` as a Job on that cluster and pushes from inside it. The vendored `hack/` set is `a2a-worker-controller`'s hardened copy — templated namespace, `case`-based value whitelisting, no service-account token — rather than `agent-claude`'s older one. The cluster arm refuses to run without an explicit `VERSION` (the Makefile default is the newest release tag, so a defaulted build would overwrite a published image with one built from a different commit) and refuses to push a `vX.Y.Z` tag from any `REF` other than that tag. `upload` and `clean` are guarded so a remote build does not fail at a push step for an image that was never local. `Dockerfile` gains a `go mod vendor` step in its build stage: the local arm got `vendor/` from `check-go-mod`, but the cluster arm clones a git ref where `vendor/` is gitignored, so `-mod=vendor` would have failed there. `make precommit` now runs `shellcheck -S warning` over `hack/*.sh`, since those scripts handle the teamvault→Secret credential path

## v0.5.14

- fix: **redact the `AnthropicAuthToken` value from the startup argument dump.** The root binary's `application` struct carried `display:"password"` — a tag the argument printer does not implement. It honours only `display:"hidden"` and `display:"length"`, so every other value fell through to the plaintext branch (`Argument: %s '%v'`) and each Job start wrote the live model-router credential in cleartext into the cluster Job log. The field now carries `display:"length"`, matching the sibling in `cmd/run-task`, so the dump names the key and its length and never the value. A regression spec drives the real printer over the real struct and fails if the redaction is removed

## v0.5.13

- test: **cover the per-prompt setup fetch, not only the push.** `v0.5.12` moved the credential to a file-backed git helper, but only the push site had a regression spec — the fetch site (the one that failed first on 2026-11-03) was pinned by nothing. The new spec starts with token `A`, lets the lifecycle refresher mint `B`, and asserts the credential `git credential fill` resolves *during* the run is `B` — the A→B shape a "file is non-empty" check would not discriminate. No production code changes

## v0.5.12

- fix: **install a file-backed git credential helper so a long lifecycle run never uses an expired token.** The GitHub App installation token lives 60 minutes and is minted once at startup; `gh auth setup-git` binds it into a helper that resolves `GH_TOKEN` from the environment of whatever runs git, and the dark-factory daemon captured that environment when it was started — so no refresh in the parent process can reach it. A token file has no such lifetime: git re-reads it at every credential lookup. Observed 2026-11-03 on `bborbe/trading#433`: token minted 18:10Z, the daemon's own `git fetch origin` refused at 19:15Z with `Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported`

## v0.5.11

- fix: **exit non-zero when the agent publishes `Status: failed`.** The result was still published to the task, but the process returned nil, so the Job completed and the executor — which records a phase success on exit 0 alone (`IsJobSucceeded` in `agent-task-executor`'s `job_watcher`) and never reads the published Status — wrote a *phase success* for a run that had failed. Once the success grace expired the task was parked at `human_review` as though a human had parked it deliberately. Observed 2026-11-03 on task `ceb79961`: a Job that published `Status: failed` for `git clone --bare: Failed to connect to github.com port 443` exited 0 and parked the task. `needs_input` is deliberately unchanged — parking for a human answer is that status's intent

## v0.5.10

- chore: update github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.138.0, github.com/bborbe/cqrs to v0.6.15, github.com/bborbe/errors to v1.6.6, github.com/bborbe/kafka to v1.29.11, github.com/bborbe/maintainer to v0.51.0, github.com/bborbe/sentry to v1.10.7, github.com/bborbe/service to v1.11.2, github.com/bborbe/time to v1.27.25, github.com/bborbe/vault-cli to v0.186.2, github.com/onsi/ginkgo/v2 to v2.34.0

## v0.5.9

- fix: re-mint the GitHub credential immediately before the push. The installation token is minted once at startup (`resolveAuth` → `githubapp.MintIAT`) and GitHub App installation tokens expire after 60 minutes, while the execution phase routinely runs longer — so the final `git push` was refused with `remote: Invalid username or token. Password authentication is not supported for Git operation`, after the implementation itself had succeeded. Measured 2026-11-02 on `bborbe/attention-controller#166`: token minted 14:54Z, push attempted 16:07Z, 73 minutes later. The execution step now calls a `refreshToken` seam right before `PushBranch` and exports the fresh value into the process env the push inherits; a refresh failure is logged and the step continues, so a short run that still holds a valid token is unaffected. The credential consumers that captured the startup token — `pkg/git`'s `cmdEnv()` and the GitHub REST client — now read the live `GH_TOKEN` first, so the refresh also reaches `headAfterPush` and ai_review's own `GetPullRequest` / worktree fetch, not only the push. **Not covered:** ai_review's Claude subprocess still receives the startup token, because its env map is built once from `resolvedToken` and the Claude runner applies an allowlist rather than inheriting `os.Environ()`. That path only matters if the review model shells `gh pr view/diff` after the 60-minute mark; the review step's own REST and git calls use the refreshed token. (`Permission to … denied` would have meant the App lacked write access — it did not, which is what ruled that out.)

## v0.5.8

- fix: pass the egress proxy environment through to git subprocesses. `cmdEnv()` returned only `HOME`, `PATH` and `GH_TOKEN`, so a clone from a sandbox that admits egress only through the allowlisting proxy dialled `github.com:443` directly and was refused by the NetworkPolicy in 2–9 ms — every dark-factory run on nuke prod failed at `planning: ensure worktree` before any LLM work started. The six proxy variables (`HTTP_PROXY`, `HTTPS_PROXY`, `NO_PROXY` and their lowercase forms) are appended when set, mirroring `github-pr-review-agent`, `github-releaser-agent` and `github-update-go-agent`, which took the same fix on 2026-10-28; an unset variable still contributes no entry, so the allowlist does not become a pass-through.

## v0.5.7

- fix: update github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.132.5 (with cqrs v0.6.13, errors v1.6.4, kafka v1.28.6, sentry v1.10.6, time v1.27.18, vault-cli v0.178.3 pulled in transitively) so the result deliverer stops restoring a stale phase. A result that advances no phase no longer republishes the Job-start phase over a park: the Kafka payload omits `phase` on those branches, so the controller's on-disk-first merge keeps the on-disk value, and the file deliverer carries the on-disk phase forward. Closes the prod-vs-sun duplicate class measured on v7.

## v0.5.6

- fix: fail a lifecycle run that is stranded in **any** non-terminal spec status, not only `prompted`. `drained()` accepts only `verifying`/`completed`, but the stall detector compared against `prompted` alone, so a spec left at `draft` or `approved` kept `drained()` false forever while nothing could advance it — the daemon logged `nothing to do, waiting for changes` and the run held its only agent slot until `activeDeadlineSeconds: 5400`. Measured 2026-10-22 17:28Z→18:34Z: spec `063-a2a-default-cluster` sat at `verifying` while a sibling spec never advanced, **45 idle iterations over ~66 min**, on v0.5.5 — a build that already contained every earlier guard, which is why the previous grace-window fix did not cover it. The detector now skips only `verifying`/`completed`/**`generating`** and reports any other status with no prompt in flight. `generating` stays excluded deliberately: dark-factory drives it and `runner/lifecycle.go` resumes or resets it after a restart, so aborting there would kill healthy work — and while **any** spec under `specs/in-progress` is `generating`, nothing is reported at all, because dark-factory generates prompts one spec at a time (`specWatcher` mutex + sequential startup scan), so a sibling legitimately waits at `approved` for the whole generation (~7 min). Flagging that sibling would abort a healthy multi-spec run 30 s in. `stallGracePolls` 3 → 10 (30 s at the 3 s poll) because `draft`/`approved` have no prompt to watch, so the grace must outlast the daemon's own pickup tick as well as the `prompted` flicker — still turning a 90-minute slot-hold into 30 seconds. The error now names the spec's real status instead of hard-coding `prompted`.

## v0.5.5

- fix: skip the ai_review worktree post-conditions when execution adopted an already-pushed branch. The adopt path routes to ai_review without creating a worktree, but ai_review checked out the task's stale `ref` and demanded every matched spec be completed there — completions the original run had already pushed to the branch, so the check could never pass and every adoption ended in `spec … is not completed (execution did not finish)`. Found on the nuke-dev replay: the run logged `"adopted": true` and then failed one step later. An adopted result now goes straight to the read-only PR verdict; the draft-PR and diff-vs-spec checks still run. Its `## Review` records only those two in `checks_passed` (with `adopted: true`) — not the `specs_completed` / `no_prompts_in_flight` gates the adopted path never evaluates, since that artifact is the human's draft→ready sign-off and must not attest to checks that did not run.

## v0.5.4

- fix: adopt an already-pushed branch head instead of re-running the whole lifecycle. A crash after `PushBranch` but before `## Result` is delivered left the remote branch ahead of the task's `ref`; the re-run repeated the full LLM job (~30 min of prompts, reproduced on nuke dev 2026-10-21) and then failed non-fast-forward with `! [rejected] HEAD -> <branch> (non-fast-forward)`, leaving a spurious failed task. The execution step now compares the remote branch head with `ref` before `EnsureWorktree`: a head that moved **and** descends from `ref` is adopted (no lifecycle, `## Result` written citing the head with `adopted: true` and `prompts_executed: 0`); a head that moved but does not descend from `ref` returns needs-input naming both shas rather than claiming another push's work.

## v0.5.3

- chore: bump the baked `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION` v0.198.9 → v0.198.11 (CLI + plugin, one pinned clone). v0.198.10 drops `model: opus` from the six `agents/*.md`, so a subagent inherits the session model instead of resolving to an Anthropic name the router maps to an adaptive-thinking-only backend, which answered every dispatch with `API Error: 400`. v0.198.11 adds `Task` to `allowed-tools` in `commands/create-prompt.md` and `commands/create-spec.md`, so the prompt-creator / spec-creator **agents** can be invoked through the Task tool; without it the command fell back to a Skill-tool call and failed with `Unknown skill: dark-factory:prompt-creator`. Both fixes reach this image through the plugin clone, which is pinned to the same tag.

## v0.5.2

- chore: update Go to 1.27.3 and github.com/bborbe/agent to v0.112.0, github.com/bborbe/kafka to v1.28.4, github.com/bborbe/sentry to v1.10.5, github.com/bborbe/vault-cli to v0.177.0

## v0.5.1

- fix: **`waitForDrain` fails fast when a requested spec is stranded at `prompted` with no prompt referencing it**, instead of holding the Job's only agent slot until the lifecycle deadline. ⚠️ dark-factory advances a spec out of `prompted` only through its spec-link scan (`CheckAndComplete`), which no-ops when no prompt carries `spec:` — so a prompt authored without the link leaves the spec unreachable and every later daemon tick a no-op. `drained()` cannot see this: it counts in-flight prompts, and a stranded run has none. Observed 2026-10-20 on nuke dev: a fallback hand-authored prompt with `spec: ""` executed to `exit_code=0`, the spec stayed `prompted`, and the run burned the whole deadline before reporting `lifecycle did not drain before deadline` over work that had actually succeeded. The new `findStalledSpec` requires three consecutive polls (9s at the 3s interval) so a healthy run — whose spec is momentarily `prompted` while its prompt is auto-approved — is never mistaken for a stalled one.

## v0.5.0

- chore: bump the baked `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION` v0.192.4 → v0.198.9 (CLI + plugin, one pinned clone). v0.198.9 makes the `spec:` link mandatory for spec-derived prompts and enforces it in the generator's `finalizePrompted`: an empty link is backfilled with an ERROR naming the file, and a batch in which no prompt links the spec now fails so the spec resets to `approved` instead of being marked `prompted`. Without it the cluster route stalls silently — the generated prompt carried no link, `CheckAndComplete` found none and no-oped, the spec sat at `prompted` forever, and the lifecycle drain burned to its deadline (nuke-dev, `bborbe/go-skeleton` PR #128, 2026-10-20). ⚠️ The jump spans six minor versions, so the CLI surface this agent drives was re-checked at the new tag: `daemon` with `--set backend=local`, `--set hideGit=true`, `--set autoGeneratePrompts=true`, `--auto-approve-prompts`, `--skip-preflight`, `--skip-healthcheck`, `--set model=…`, plus `spec complete <id>` — all present.

## v0.4.7

- fix: **Go 1.27.2 now passes `make precommit`.** The standalone `errcheck:` and `gosec:` targets are both retired and dropped from `check:`, and both linters now run embedded in golangci-lint, which `.golangci.yml` already enabled. `GOLANGCI_LINT_VERSION` moves v2.13.1 → v2.14.0, the `go` directive and `Dockerfile` move to 1.27.2, and `golang.org/x/net` moves v0.58.0 → v0.60.0. ⚠️ **Neither target was repairable, which is why both are removed rather than repointed.** `go run github.com/kisielk/errcheck@v1.20.0` and `go run github.com/securego/gosec/v2/cmd/gosec@$(GOSEC_VERSION)` each build in their **own** module context, pinning a `golang.org/x/tools` reader that stops at export-data version 4 while the 1.27.2 toolchain emits version 5, so each dies with `internal error: package "X" without types was imported` at any `go.mod` directive. Dropping the `@$(ERRCHECK_VERSION)` pin does not rescue it either: `precommit` runs `ensure` → `go mod tidy` first, and tidy strips a require nothing imports. ⚠️ **Coverage is preserved, not traded away.** `.golangci.yml` gains `settings.errcheck.exclude-functions` carrying the retired target's `-ignore '(Close|Write|Fprint)'` list, and `settings.gosec.excludes: [G104]` carrying `-exclude=G104`. The `go` directive bump is load-bearing rather than tidy: it is what clears the nine `stdlib@v1.27.1 -> v1.27.2` advisories that `osv-scanner` reports, and it could not move while the standalone targets ran. Also bumps `osv-scanner` v2.3.1 → v2.6.0: the pinned v2.3.1 panics during call-graph analysis in `golang.org/x/tools@v0.38.0/go/ssa`, and v2.6.0 carries a fixed x/tools.

## v0.4.6

- fix: `make build` refuses to stamp a version onto a tree that is not that version's tag (`check-version-tag`, escape hatch `ALLOW_UNTAGGED_BUILD=1`). `VERSION` defaults to the newest tag repo-wide, so an operator-run build from an untagged or older tree silently republishes under the newest tag. The guard compares `git describe --exact-match HEAD` against `$(VERSION)` and exits non-zero on mismatch.

## v0.4.0

- fix: raise the lifecycle timeout default 30m→90m and make it configurable, so real multi-prompt feature runs (generation ~7m + per-prompt execute 10-15m + fix loops) no longer hit the deadline mid-execution. New `LIFECYCLE_TIMEOUT` env override (Go duration) sets the deployment default; a per-task `lifecycle_timeout_minutes:` frontmatter field overrides for that task only. Both are resolved via `ResolveLifecycleTimeoutFromEnv` / `ResolveLifecycleTimeout` and threaded through `NewExecutionRunnerWithTimeout`. Invalid/absent values fall back safely (never zero).
- fix: handle ignored `os.Setenv`/`os.Unsetenv` error returns in the lifecycle-timeout tests so the standalone errcheck target passes.
- fix: unexport `resolveLifecycleTimeoutFromEnv`/`resolveLifecycleTimeout` (factory-pattern rule — internal helpers, test access via `export_test.go` aliases) and lowercase the env-parse warning messages, per bot review.

## v0.3.11

- chore: update Go to 1.26.6 and dependencies; fix GO-2026-5841 (klauspost/compress), GO-2026-6179 (golang.org/x/mod), GO-2026-6180 (golang.org/x/mod), GO-2026-5026 (stdlib), GO-2026-5972 (stdlib), GO-2026-6090 (stdlib), GO-2026-6218 (stdlib)

## v0.3.10

- fix: fail-fast on a permanently-failed prompt instead of hanging to the lifecycle deadline. When a dark-factory prompt exhausts its retries the failure handler leaves it in `prompts/in-progress` with `status: failed` and the scanner skips it forever ("queue blocked until manual retry"), so its spec can never reach `verifying`. `drained()` could not distinguish that dead prompt from a slow one, so `waitForDrain` spun until the 30-minute `lifecycleTimeout` — and in-cluster the overall-run budget hard-killed the Job with `context canceled` at ~30 min BEFORE the step could escalate, so no `## Failure` was ever written and the task was not cleanly parked. `waitForDrain` now scans `prompts/in-progress` each tick via new `findFailedPrompt` and returns a lifecycle error the moment a prompt reaches terminal `status: failed`, surfacing its `lastFailReason`. The execution step then escalates cleanly (`Status: failed`) within seconds while the context is still alive — PR stays draft, spec stays incomplete, task parks. Approved/executing/unparseable prompts are ignored (only terminal `failed` counts). Unit tests cover the detector's discrimination + the RunLifecycle fast-path timing.

## v0.3.9

- fix: commit the spec-completion move before pushing, so completed specs actually reach the PR branch. `dark-factory spec complete` (which the execution step drives after the daemon stops) rewrites the working tree — moving the spec `specs/in-progress → specs/completed` — but does NOT git-commit it (nothing commits it once the daemon is gone, unlike the daemon's per-prompt `workflow:direct` commits). `PushBranch` is a bare `git push HEAD`, so the completion was silently dropped: the PR kept an approved-not-completed spec, the watcher re-emitted the task on the agent's own push, and runs overlapped indefinitely (self-trigger loop). New `ExecutionRunner.CommitSpecChanges` stages `specs/` and commits after `completeSpecs` and before `PushBranch` (no-op when nothing is staged). Now the completed spec lands on the branch → the watcher stops re-triggering → clean multi-spec drain to `human_review`. Unit tests cover the commit + the no-op path and assert the execution step calls it before pushing.

## v0.3.8

- fix: `RunLifecycle` no longer stops the dark-factory daemon while a generated prompt is still awaiting auto-approval. The drain check (`drained()`) only looked at `prompts/in-progress`, ignoring the generation **inbox** (`prompts/*.md` at the repo root, where a freshly generated prompt waits for the daemon's auto-approve audit). Because the daemon flips the spec to `verifying` while that audit runs, `drained()` returned true mid-audit, `stopDaemon` SIGKILLed the in-flight audit subprocess (`auto-approve: audit FAILED ... signal: killed`), the prompt was never approved/executed, and the implementation file (e.g. the `HELLO_DARK_FACTORY.md` marker) was never created — ai_review then correctly escalated on the absent file. New `hasInboxPrompts` gates the drain on the inbox too, so the lifecycle waits for the prompt to be approved → executed → completed. Surfaced on go-skeleton PR #40 (master `.dark-factory.yaml` sets `validationPrompt: docs/dod.md`, making the audit slow enough to lose the race). Unit test drives a stub daemon that leaves a prompt in the inbox and asserts the lifecycle does not drain.

## v0.3.7

- fix: inject the fleet model into the backend:local daemon. The execution step now forwards the configured model (`claudelib.ClaudeModel`, from the pod's `ANTHROPIC_MODEL`) to `dark-factory daemon` as `--set model=<model>` via `NewExecutionStep`'s new constructor arg — no `os.Getenv` inside the step. The daemon resolves its model from `--set` > `.dark-factory.yaml` `model:` > a built-in Claude default; because it does NOT read `ANTHROPIC_MODEL` for its own selection, a target repo whose `.dark-factory.yaml` omits `model:` silently ran on Sonnet (a ToU violation), which on go-skeleton PR #40 produced a prompt asserting the wrong byte count and never committed the marker. Injecting the model makes the fleet model authoritative regardless of per-repo config. Unit test asserts the flag is forwarded.

## v0.3.6

- fix: ai_review no longer flags dark-factory's own bookkeeping as out-of-scope. The read-only diff-vs-spec reviewer (`pkg/prompts/review.md`) now excludes pipeline-metadata paths — `prompts/**`, `specs/**`, and `.dark-factory.yaml` — from its scope judgment, since the lifecycle necessarily commits them on every run (generated prompts, in-progress→completed moves). Previously a correct implementation escalated to `failed` at ai_review because a spec constraint like "No other file is modified" can never hold for this pipeline (observed in cluster E2E: the marker was created correctly but the reviewer flagged the prompt/spec churn). The reviewer now judges only real implementation files against the spec. Verified via the local `cmd/run-task` loop against a clean draft PR: the same scenario now returns `pass` → `human_review`.
- chore: `go mod tidy` records `github.com/maxbrunsfeld/counterfeiter/v6` as an indirect dependency.
- chore: bump `golang.org/x/text` v0.38.0 → v0.39.0 (indirect) — clears CVE-2026-56852 (infinite loop on invalid input) flagged by trivy.

## v0.3.5

- chore: bump baked `DARK_FACTORY_VERSION` v0.192.0 → v0.192.4 (CLI + plugin). v0.192.4 fixes the `generate-prompts-for-spec` command's hardcoded `/workspace` paths (docker-mount convention) → cwd-relative, so backend:local generation writes prompts into the worktree the daemon watches instead of an empty `/workspace`. Unblocks the backend:local generation→execution lifecycle.

## v0.3.4

- fix: populate remote-tracking refs (`refs/remotes/origin/*`) in the RepoManager's bare clone. `git clone --bare` maps remote branches to `refs/heads/*`, so `origin/master` never resolved in a worktree — and dark-factory's per-prompt "sync with default branch" (`git merge origin/<default>`, run by every workflow) failed with `origin/master - not something we can merge`, stalling execution after generation. New `configureRemoteTracking` sets the standard `+refs/heads/*:refs/remotes/origin/*` refspec and fetches, on both the clone and update paths.

## v0.3.3

- fix: bake the `coding` plugin into the runtime image (Dockerfile), alongside the existing `dark-factory` plugin. dark-factory's generation step invokes the prompt-creator agent, which uses the `coding` plugin's Go guides to write prompt files; without it the fleet's MiniMax model (`MiniMax-M2.7-highspeed`) produced no prompt file ("generation produced no prompt files") and the spec never left `approved`. Local runs generate fine because the operator's `~/.claude` already has `coding`; the cluster image did not. Mirrors github-pr-review-agent's build-time `coding` install.

## v0.3.2

- fix: stream the `dark-factory` daemon's stdout/stderr to the agent's own stdout in `dark_factory_runner.startDaemon` (was `cmd.Stdout/Stderr = nil`, i.e. discarded). The backend:local lifecycle — and the claude subprocesses the daemon spawns — is now visible in `kubectl logs`. Without it a hung daemon (e.g. a claude call blocking on a no-TTY onboarding prompt) was indistinguishable from slow progress until the 30-minute lifecycle deadline. Writes to the process stdout/stderr, not a repo file, so it is not swept into the daemon's commits.

## v0.3.1

- fix: hoist `ARG CLAUDE_YOLO_IMAGE` to global scope (before the first `FROM`) in the Dockerfile. It was declared inside the build stage, so the runtime `FROM ${CLAUDE_YOLO_IMAGE}` could not interpolate it and BuildKit aborted with "base name should not be blank" — `make buca` failed before any push. CI runs `make precommit` (go build/test/lint), never `docker build`, so this latent bug surfaced only on the first real image build.
- fix: build the dark-factory CLI from the pinned clone (`go install .` in the module root) instead of `go install github.com/bborbe/dark-factory@${DARK_FACTORY_VERSION}`. dark-factory's `go.mod` carries `exclude` directives, which `go install pkg@version` refuses; building from the module root honors them (same as upstream `make install`). Reuses the clone the runtime image already makes for the plugin marketplace, so there is now a single pinned clone for both CLI and plugin. Both fixes verified with a local `make build`.

## v0.3.0

- feat: add GitHub App authentication. When `APP_ID`, `INSTALLATION_ID`, and a PEM (`PEM_KEY_FILE` or `PEM_KEY`) are all set, the agent mints a short-lived installation access token at startup (`githubapp.MintIAT`) and forwards it to every git/gh subprocess — `os.Setenv("GH_TOKEN", …)` covers the dark-factory daemon's `git push` (inherits `os.Environ()`), `gh auth setup-git` installs the git credential helper, and the token is threaded into the RepoManager, GitHub REST client, and gh-token preflight. Falls back to the raw `GH_TOKEN` input when App creds are absent so local `cmd/run-task` (with `GH_TOKEN=$(gh auth token)`) keeps working; errors clearly when neither is configured. Fixes cluster clone/push failures where the pod set no `GH_TOKEN`. Copies `pkg/githubauth` (the `gh auth setup-git` configurator) from github-pr-review-agent.

- fix: add `--set hideGit=true` to the execution step's dark-factory flags — the RepoManager runs the lifecycle in a git worktree (`.git` is a file), which trips dark-factory's spec-084 worktree safety gate; without this the daemon refuses to start. Validated in the local E2E: the daemon now starts and runs inside the worktree.
- fix: install the dark-factory Claude PLUGIN in the runtime image (Dockerfile), not just the CLI binary. The backend:local lifecycle runs `/dark-factory:generate-prompts-for-spec` and `/dark-factory:audit-prompt` *inside* claude; with only the CLI installed, claude reports `Unknown command` → zero prompts generated → the spec silently resets to `approved` and the daemon idles (the E2E root cause, 2026-07-13). Mirrors github-pr-review-agent's build-time `coding` plugin install. **Pinned** to the same `${DARK_FACTORY_VERSION}` tag as the CLI (clone that tag + add as a local marketplace, not marketplace HEAD) so the plugin minor cannot drift from the CLI minor. Confirmed locally: with the plugin installed, generation produces a valid prompt.
- docs: record two backend:local provisioning requirements in design.md Part 5 — (1) the dark-factory plugin must be installed in the runtime `CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR`; (2) backend:local ignores dark-factory `config.env`, so the model-router `ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL` + auth token must be pod env vars (a spec-104 follow-up gap).

## v0.2.0

- feat: implement Increment 1 of the three-phase implementer — wire planning/execution/ai_review as distinct phases (domain.TaskPhase constants), route the `dark-factory-implement` task type; add RepoManager (bare-clone cache + per-task worktree), claude-auth + gh-token preflight steps, and the pure-Go planning step (clone + precondition scan: ref==PR head, PR draft, `.dark-factory.yaml` present, approved-not-completed spec in the PR diff → writes `## Plan`, routes execution; escalates without mutating assignee/status); wire `cmd/run-task` as a local per-phase harness. Execution/ai_review are stubs (Increments 2/3).
- feat: implement Increment 2 — the execution step drives the dark-factory backend:local lifecycle. Live investigation established the correct one-worktree invocation: `dark-factory daemon --set backend=local --set autoGeneratePrompts=true --auto-approve-prompts --skip-preflight --skip-healthcheck` (backgrounded → poll-until-drained → kill; one-shot `run` does NOT generate — generation is daemon-only), then `dark-factory spec complete <id>` (no auto-complete), then `git push`. Adds `pkg/dark_factory_runner.go` (`ExecutionRunner` seam over daemon/spec-complete/push) and replaces the execution stub: idempotent (`## Result` present → route ai_review), config via `--set`/flags never committed to the branch, fail-closed when a spec never reaches `verifying`/`completed` (prompt failed DoD/audit), writes typed `## Result`, routes ai_review — all without mutating assignee/status.
- feat: implement Increment 3 — the ai_review step (custom verdict-routing, read-only). A deterministic gate re-checks post-conditions (PR still draft, every matched spec completed, no prompts in-flight) and escalates (`failed`) on violation; then a read-only Claude diff-vs-spec review emits a typed `## Review` verdict. Pass → `Done, human_review` (the human's draft→ready flip is the sign-off); concerns → `failed` (escalate). NEVER runs `gh pr ready`; never clears assignee (the controller does at human_review). Completes the three-phase implementer agent logic (planning → execution → ai_review).

## v0.1.3

15	// the GitHub REST API) or a local sandbox repo.

42		os.Exit(service.Main(context.Background(), app, &app.SentryDSN, &app.SentryProxy))
